subject: Staged deletion runbook + proof-of-deletion & rollback escape hatch
body:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Sara Quinn <sara.quinn@brightside.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged deletion runbook + proof-of-deletion & rollback escape hatch

Hi Sara —

Following up on our call this morning. Attached is our proposed 'staged deletion' runbook that maps to the DPA retention sections and subprocessors (brief summary below). We want to make sure the Brightside security and legal teams have the artifacts they need for sign-off on the deletion cadence and backup purge timelines.

Key asks:
- Confirm whether a 30-day rollback window (for operational rollback during a confirmed incident) is acceptable if we provide cryptographic proof-of-deletion and a secure snapshot escrow.
- Confirm the required retention for audit logs (we propose 90 days for high-fidelity logs, 365 for aggregated metrics).
- Any additional evidence types Brightside needs to accept deletion (hash manifests, signed attestations, or chain-of-custody logs).

Proposed short timeline (high level):
- Day 0: Deletion request accepted and queued.
- Day 1–7: Live data purge and KV-store compaction.
- Day 8–30: Backups flagged for retention/hold; no external restore allowed unless a verified rollback request with executive approval.
- Day 31–45: Secure backup purge window (final deletion from backups, followed by post-purge attestations).

Attachments: deletion_runbook_v1.md (runbook), evidence_proof_template.csv (hash manifest).

If you prefer, we can gate the escape hatch behind a two-person signoff from Brightside (security + legal) and a short SLA for Redwood to provide proof artifacts.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: deletion_runbook_v1.md (text/markdown)]

-----
On Thu, Mar 30, 2028 at 09:48 AM Sara Quinn <sara.quinn@brightside.ai> wrote:

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the runbook. Quick first-pass comments from Brightside legal/security: we appreciate the staged approach but need clarity on two points before DPA counter-signature:

1) Proof-of-deletion: we need a verifiable artifact that proves deletion from backups (not just a log entry). Is the hash manifest approach you attached intended to be published to us, or retained internally with a signed attestation?

2) Cross-border backups: our data residency requires any EU-origin data to be deleted within the same timeline and we need assurance that subprocessor transfers are limited. Can you list subprocessors holding backups and their locations?

We have a few redlines in the PDF — attaching. Also, we would like the escape-hatch window to be explicit in the DPA as an exception clause.

Sara
Sara Quinn
Head of Security, Brightside Labs
[Attachment: brightside_dpa_redlines.pdf (application/pdf)]

-----
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sara Quinn <sara.quinn@brightside.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged deletion runbook + proof-of-deletion & rollback escape hatch

Sara —

Appreciate the quick review. Short answers to your questions:

1) Proof-of-deletion model: we propose providing both the hash manifest (CSV) and a signed attestation document. Process: after final backup purge we publish a signed proof-of-deletion package via a secure link (GPG-signed manifest + internal audit id). Brightside can verify manifests against the attestation. If you prefer third-party attestation (forensic vendor), we can add that as an optional one-time step.

2) Subprocessors and locations: current backup subprocessors are listed in section 4 of the runbook: VendorCloud (us-east-1), Glacier Mirror (eu-west-1), and EdgeRecovery (ap-southeast-1). For EU-origin records we will ensure EU-hosted snapshots are purged per the same schedule and we can provide export logs scoped by region.

Mitigations we can offer (to minimize risk):
- Escrow snapshot retained in a segregated S3 bucket with narrow ACLs for 30 days.
- Read-only immutable snapshot copies for the rollback window (no restores without two-person Brightside signoff).
- Extended, tamper-evident audit logs covering deletion operations for 90 days (hash-chaining).

If Brightside accepts those mitigations we can add a short DPA clause that describes the escape-hatch process and signoff requirements (two signatories, max 30-day rollback). Laura — can you confirm security acceptance of the hash-chaining approach?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security Operations
[Attachment: evidence_proof_template.csv (text/csv)]

-----
On Thu, Mar 30, 2028 at 11:05 AM Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:

Stephanie / Alex / Sara —

I reviewed the hash-chaining and the escrow snapshot proposal. Security is comfortable with the scheme provided we add the following controls:

- Immutable snapshots must be stored with object-lock enabled and customer-specific encryption keys managed via Brightside's KMS when requested.
- Any restore request during the 30-day rollback window triggers an automated audit ticket and requires two Brightside signoffs and one Redwood manager-level approval (audit trail kept).
- For EU-origin data, we will not replicate EU snapshots to non-EU subprocessors during the hold period; those snapshots are handled by Glacier Mirror (eu-west-1).

Procurement note: please coordinate DPA language for the escape-hatch with Rishi — we need a simple clause and a clear timeline so there is no ambiguity later.

Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: VendorCloud Procurement <procure@vendorcloud.com>, Sara Quinn <sara.quinn@brightside.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged deletion runbook + proof-of-deletion & rollback escape hatch

All —

Thanks for the thread. From a contracting/procurement perspective I can accept the 30-day rollback escape hatch as long as:

1) The DPA includes a short, enumerated exception clause (we'll circulate language).
2) Brightside agrees to the two-person signoff (security + legal) or a named delegate.
3) We confirm a final procurement item: a PO for the escrow storage if Brightside asks us to host the enclosed snapshot under Redwood custody.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi to send DPA addendum language (one-page) for review by EOD Monday.
- Alex to provide a final list of subprocessors and region maps in the Drive folder.
- Sara/Matt to confirm whether Brightside will require third-party attestation (forensic vendor) or accept Redwood-signed attestation.

Procurement contact for VendorCloud (backup subproc) is CC'd — please provide a current subprocessor location matrix and any SOC reports we can share.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal & Procurement, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-dpa-addendum-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

---

Summary: we have alignment on the technical controls and evidence artifacts. Remaining open items are: (1) finalize DPA clause language, (2) confirm whether Brightside needs an external attestation, and (3) procure a PO if escrow storage remains under Redwood custody.

I'll follow up with the DPA addendum soon.

--
Alex Martinez
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
